steps.note: Right clicking a layer row has always given a menu; right clicking the same layer on the picture gave nothing. This walk right clicks the boxes themselves. It shows that a right click on a box nobody has picked picks it first, that right clicking one of two picked boxes offers Group and makes one group of both, and that a right click on the bare picture gives the picture's own commands rather than an empty menu.
nothing was picked; right clicking the middle box picked it and opened its own menu, the same rows the layer row menu has always carried
two boxes picked on the picture, the way a person picks the things they want held together
right clicking one of the two moved nothing: the menu is about both, and it carries Group with Command G printed against it
Group out of the canvas menu did exactly what Command G does: the two picked boxes went into one group and the third was left alone, so the list is a group and a rectangle
Ungroup from the same menu put the two boxes back loose, exactly where they were
a right click where there is no layer is not an empty menu and not a menu about a layer that is not there: it is the picture's own commands, on the same shortcuts the menu bar prints for them
Select All then Deselect, both taken from the bare picture's own menu; Deselect is only there while there is a marked region to drop, which is why it is asked for second
